project.objective: Did Chresten Nielsen and his wife Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter of Tyrsted, Vejle, Denmark have a daughter named Birte, born 1805, in addition to their nine known children (b. 1791-1801)?

questions.question: Do the Tyrsted parish registers (Vejle, Denmark) record a baptism for a daughter named Birte born to Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter around 1805?
questions.rationale: The objective asks whether Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter had a daughter named Birte born 1805 beyond their nine known children (b. 1791–1801). Danish Lutheran parish baptism registers (kirkebøger) are the primary source for child births in this jurisdiction and period; Tyrsted parish in Vejle amt would have recorded any baptism in that household. Confirming or negating this specific baptism entry is the most direct path to answering the objective. A locality survey of Tyrsted/Vejle record holdings is needed first to identify which collections are available and indexed.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Two genuinely independent FamilySearch church records for Tyrsted parish confirm that Birte (born 3 Aug 1805, christened 6 Oct 1805) is the daughter of Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter: (1) the 1805 baptism index (src_001, derivative from the Tyrsted kirkebog 007226375_002_M9DY-VFQ); and (2) the 1819 confirmation index (src_003, derivative from the same volume's confirmation register), which independently names Birte Christensd (born 1805, confirmed 18 Apr 1819, Tyrsted) as daughter of Christen Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensd. The original baptism register image (src_002) was examined via fast OCR, confirming name, birth location (Dallerup), and mother name; Opus re-read was blocked at 1.6 MB (genuine tool inaccessibility). Burial records (negative: no early death found), 1787 census (negative: not indexed for Tyrsted), and probate indexes (negative: no coverage for area) were all searched. Pre-civil-registration Denmark (registration began 1851) leaves no additional record type that would authoritatively confirm or deny a 1805 birth.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: YES — two independent Tyrsted church records (baptism 1805, confirmation 1819) name Birte as daughter of Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter, directly answering whether this 10th child existed.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: YES — FamilySearch searched across baptism, confirmation, original register image, burial (collection 1520593), 1787 census (collection 2790466), 1801 census (not indexed for child born 1805 anyway), and probate indexes (collection 2026233). Pre-1793 browse-only volume (0% indexed) skipped; does not cover the 1805 birth and would not affect the conclusion.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: SUBSTANTIALLY MET — Original baptism register image examined via image_transcribe (fast OCR); Opus re-read blocked at 1.6 MB (tool inaccessibility — not an unsearched gap). Confirmation register original image not accessed, but two independently consistent derivative indexes reduce overturn risk from this limitation.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: YES — src_001 (baptism record, 1805) and src_003 (confirmation record, 1819) are genuinely independent: different events, 14 years apart, different register sections, recorded by the Tyrsted pastor in different circumstances. They agree on all key facts: child name Birte, birth year 1805, parish Tyrsted, father Chresten/Christen Nielsen, mother Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: YES — src_001 carries primary information for the christening and birth date (parish officiant + presenting parents at baptism); src_003 carries primary information for the confirmation event and parentage statement (officiating pastor). Both are classified as derivative source records (indexes derived from the kirkebog).
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: NO CONFLICTS — All sources are internally consistent. 'Børte'/'Birte', 'Christen'/'Chresten', and 'Sørensd'/'Sørensdatter' are standard Danish orthographic variants, not substantive discrepancies. The OCR gap on the father's name in a_017 is resolved by primary direct evidence in a_022 and a_024 from the confirmation record.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: LOW — No Danish civil birth registration before 1851 exists to contradict or supplement these church records. Census records predate Birte's birth (1787, 1801) or were not searched for later years (1834+, which could show Birte as an adult but would not overturn the established parentage). Probate indexes do not cover Tyrsted for this period. No plausible unsearched source would name a different parent for a child born in Tyrsted in 1805.

items.jurisdiction: Tyrsted Parish, Hatting Herred, Vejle Amt, Denmark
items.rationale: Denmark, Baptisms, 1618-1923 (collection 1778463) holds 2,633 indexed Tyrsted records per the Vejle County Baptisms Coverage Table. The 1793-1823 Tyrsted kirkebog (imageGroup 007226375_002_M9DY-VFQ) is 43% indexed in this collection. A search for a daughter named Birte (also try Nielsdatter) with father Chresten Nielsen, c. 1802-1808, is the fastest and most direct path to confirming or ruling out the putative 1805 birth. Also search the broader Denmark, Church Records, 1484-1941 (collection 2078555, index + images) as a parallel check since it covers the same period with different indexing. Note: per Danish patronymic convention, the daughter would be indexed as Birte Nielsdatter, not Birte Nielsen.

The 1793-1823 Tyrsted kirkebog (imageGroup 007226375_002_M9DY-VFQ, 131 images) is only 43% indexed — approximately half the pages are not name-searchable and must be browsed image by image. If pli_001 (indexed search) finds no Birte, browse this volume's baptism section for c. 1804-1808 to catch any record the index missed. Arkivalieronline (arkivalieronline.rigsarkivet.dk) provides free image access to Tyrsted church books as an alternative if FamilySearch images are unavailable. Use the image-reader skill to read individual pages.

The pre-1793 Tyrsted kirkebog (imageGroup 007226375_001_M9DY-VF3, 212 images, 0% indexed — browse-only) covers 1684-1796 and is needed to verify births of the nine known children born 1791-1793 under the Stjernholm-era jurisdiction. Browsing the baptism section for 1791-1793 establishes the family baseline (confirming Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine as parents), and confirms no Birte was born before the jurisdiction boundary change. Records from before 1793 are filed under Stjernholm amt; do not expect them in Vejle-era indexed collections.

The 1787 Denmark census (FamilySearch collection 2790466, indexed) predates the nine known children and would show Chresten Nielsen's household at that time — confirming his identity, residence in Tyrsted, and his wife Birte Kirstine. This contextual anchor ensures we are researching the correct Chresten Nielsen before relying on baptism entries.

The 1801 Denmark census (Ancestry collection 61726, also at Danish State Archives sa.dk) falls between the last known child (b. 1801) and the putative 1805 daughter. It would enumerate all household members as of 1801, confirming the nine known children and showing that Birte (if born 1805) does not yet exist — providing a clean compositional snapshot against which the 1805 baptism (if found) can be assessed. This census is NOT indexed on FamilySearch and requires Ancestry access or the State Archives portal.

If a baptism for a daughter Birte is found (pli_001 or pli_002), search Denmark, Burials, 1640-1917 (collection 1520593, indexed) for Birte Nielsdatter in Tyrsted, c. 1805-1825, to determine whether she died in infancy or childhood. A burial record would explain her absence from the 1834+ censuses and serve as corroborating evidence that she was born but did not survive to adulthood. A negative result (no burial found) strengthens the case that she lived into adulthood and warrants further follow-up.

items.jurisdiction: Tyrsted, Hatting Herred, Vejle Amt, Denmark
items.rationale: Denmark, Probate Indexes, 1674-1851 (FamilySearch collection 2026233, indexed) may contain an estate record for Chresten Nielsen or Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter. Probate documents in early 19th-century Denmark often enumerate heirs by name, which would directly confirm or rule out a daughter named Birte among the children. This is an important FAN/contextual source applying BCG Standard 14 breadth beyond vital records.

Birte (born 3 Aug 1805) would have been confirmed at age 14-16, i.e. approximately 1819-1821. A confirmation record in Denmark, Church Records 1484-1941 (collection 2078555) — which IS indexed for Tyrsted confirmations in this period — would be a genuinely independent corroboration of her existence: different event (confirmation vs. baptism), different year, different register section, created by the Tyrsted pastor at a different time. This is the strongest independent verification available within FamilySearch given that the 1801 census cannot show a child born 1805 and the probate indexes don't cover the area.

hypotheses.claim: The 1805 Tyrsted baptism entry naming 'Chresten Nielsen' as father of Birte might refer to a second Chresten Nielsen household in Tyrsted parish whose wife was Sidsel Lausdr, not Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter
hypotheses.ruled_out_reason: The baptism record (src_001) names the mother as 'Birte Kirstine' (a_009), which is directly inconsistent with the second Chresten Nielsen household whose wife was Sidsel Lausdr. The conjunction of father name 'Chresten Nielsen' (a_006) and mother name 'Birte Kirstine' (a_009) uniquely identifies the subject's parents, eliminating the alternative household. The 1819 confirmation record (src_003) independently corroborates both parent names ('Christen Nielsen' + 'Birte Kirstine Sørensd'), providing a second cross-time authentication of the household identification.
hypotheses.notes: At least two men named Chresten/Christen Nielsen were heads of household in Tyrsted parish in the early 19th century; a_006 (father name in baptism record) created the ambiguity; a_009 (mother name 'Birte Kirstine', inconsistent with Sidsel Lausdr) resolves it.

Pre-1793 Tyrsted kirkebog (imageGroup 007226375_001, 0% indexed) was not searched — browse-only, and does not cover the 1805 birth. proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Birte Christensdatter, Born 1805 — Daughter of Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter of Tyrsted, Vejle, Denmark

### Research Question

Did Chresten Nielsen and his wife Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter of Tyrsted, Vejle, Denmark have a daughter named Birte, born 1805, in addition to their nine known children (born 1791–1801)?

### Conclusion

The preponderance of evidence strongly suggests that **Birte Christensdatter, born 3 August 1805 at Dallerup in Tyrsted parish, Vejle, Denmark, was the daughter of Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter** — a tenth child in addition to the nine known children born between 1791 and 1801.

---

### Primary Evidence

**1. Baptism Index, 1805 (derivative/primary/direct)**

The FamilySearch-indexed baptism record in "Denmark, Baptisms, 1618-1923" (collection 1778463) records a daughter named Birte, born 3 August 1805 at Dallerup and christened 6 October 1805 at Tyrsted, Vejle, Denmark, naming the father as Chresten Nielsen and the mother as Birte Kirstine.¹ This is a **derivative** source — an index compiled from the Tyrsted Lutheran parish register (kirkebog, vol. 007226375_002_M9DY-VFQ, 1793–1823). The information it contains is **primary**: the child's name, sex, birth date, christening date, birthplace, and parentage were recorded at or near the time of the christening by the parish officiant and presenting parents. The evidence is **direct** — the facts answer the research question without requiring inference.

**2. Original Parish Register Image, 1805 (original/primary/direct — partial read)**

The original Tyrsted kirkebog, image 007226375_00232 (imageGroup 007226375_002_M9DY-VFQ), was examined via fast OCR.² The OCR confirmed the child's name ("Birte"), the birth location ("Dallerup"), and the August 1805 date. The mother's name was read as "Børte Kirstine" — a common orthographic variant of "Birte Kirstine" in 18th–19th-century Danish records, consistent with the derivative index. The OCR was unable to clearly resolve the father's name column for the August 3 entry, due to column-alignment drift — this is an OCR limitation, not evidence of a different father. A full Opus-class re-read was blocked by image size (1.6 MB). This source is **original** and its information **primary**, but the read is acknowledged as partial.

**3. Confirmation Index, 1819 (derivative/primary+secondary/direct — independent)**

Fourteen years after the baptism, the Tyrsted parish confirmation register — indexed in "Danmark Kirkebøger, 1484-1941" (collection 2078555) — records "Birte Christensd," born 1805, confirmed 18 April 1819 at Tyrsted, Vejle, Denmark, with the father named as Christen Nielsen and the mother as Birte Kirstine Sørensd.³ This source is **derivative** (an index from the Tyrsted kirkebog). The confirmation event is **primary** information (recorded at the time of the ceremony by the officiating pastor); the birth year 1805 is **secondary** (recorded 14 years after the birth, from the pastor's knowledge or reference to the baptism register). The parentage statement is **direct** evidence.

This record is **genuinely independent** of the baptism records: it documents a different ecclesiastical event (confirmation vs. baptism), created 14 years later by the Tyrsted pastor in a different register section. It independently attests the child's birth year and parentage.

---

### Name Variants — Not Conflicts

Three apparent differences between sources are orthographic variants, not substantive discrepancies:

- **Birte / Børte**: "Børte" in the OCR of the original image is the same name as "Birte" — a common 19th-century Danish spelling variant reflecting the same given name. The baptism index and confirmation index both use "Birte."
- **Chresten / Christen**: The confirmation index names the father "Christen Nielsen"; the baptism index names him "Chresten Nielsen." Both are standard Danish spellings of the same given name (from "Christian"), reflecting dialect and scribal preference. No conflict.
- **Christensd / Christensdatter / Sørensd / Sørensdatter**: The confirmation index abbreviates both the child's and the mother's patronymic surname — "Christensd" for Christensdatter, "Sørensd" for Sørensdatter — consistent with standard Danish index abbreviation practice. No conflict.

---

### Negative Evidence

No burial record for Birte Christensdatter (daughter of Chresten Nielsen) was found in Denmark Burials, 1640-1917 (collection 1520593) for 1805–1825, consistent with her having survived infancy. The 1787 Danish census (collection 2790466) returned no results for Chresten Nielsen in Tyrsted or Vejle, likely due to limited indexing coverage; in any case this census predates Birte's birth and cannot confirm or deny her existence. The Denmark Probate Indexes, 1674-1851 (collection 2026233) returned no results, suggesting the collection lacks coverage for Tyrsted in this period. The 1801 Danish census was searched on FamilySearch without finding the family in indexed results; as Birte was not born until 1805, the 1801 census could not in any case directly confirm her existence.

---

### Identity Disambiguation — Two Chresten Nielsen Households

The patronymic surname "Nielsen" and the given name "Chresten" were both common in 19th-century Tyrsted parish; research identified at least one other head of household in Tyrsted with the same name — a Chresten Nielsen whose wife was Sidsel Lausdr. The identity of the father in the subject's baptism entry is established, and that alternative household eliminated, by the conjunction of the father's name (a_006: "Chresten Nielsen") and the mother's name (a_009: "Birte Kirstine") stated in the baptism record: the second household had a different wife entirely, and no record places a Birte born 1805 in that household. The 1819 confirmation record (src_003) independently supplies both parent names ("Christen Nielsen" + "Birte Kirstine Sørensd"), providing a second cross-time authentication of the correct household identification across a 14-year gap.

---

### Limitations and Path to Proved

The conclusion reaches **probable** rather than **proved** because the confirmation register original image was not accessed — only the derivative index (src_003) was examined for that second independent source. The GPS standard for a **proved** conclusion requires two or more independent **original** records with primary information; only one original record (the baptism register image) was examined here, and that examination was partial due to OCR tool constraints. If the Tyrsted kirkebog confirmation register image (imageGroup 007226375_002_M9DY-VFQ, approximately pages 180–200 for 1819 entries) were examined and confirmed the parentage statement, the tier could advance to proved.

---

### Tier Declaration

Based on two independent corroborating sources — the 1805 Tyrsted baptism record and the 1819 Tyrsted confirmation record — with no conflicting evidence found across six record types and repositories, with the alternative Chresten Nielsen/Sidsel Lausdr household in Tyrsted explicitly eliminated by the stated mother's name, and with research declared reasonably exhaustive, the evidence **strongly suggests** that Birte Christensdatter (born 3 August 1805, Dallerup, Tyrsted parish, Vejle, Denmark) is the daughter of Chresten Nielsen and Birte Kirstine Sørensdatter — a tenth child of this couple in addition to their nine known children born 1791–1801. **Tier: Probable.**

---

¹ "Denmark, Baptisms, 1618-1923," database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:W6M7-SWMM : 23 June 2020), Entry for Birte; citing Tyrsted, Vejle, Denmark; FHL microfilm.

² Tyrsted Parish Register (Kirkebog), 1793–1823, vol. 2, image 007226375_00232, baptism entry Aug 3, 1805 (Birte, Dallerup); imageGroup 007226375_002_M9DY-VFQ; Tyrsted parish, Hatting herred, Vejle amt, Denmark; digital image, FamilySearch (familysearch.org), accessed 2026-07-31.

³ "Danmark Kirkebøger, 1484-1941," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QG8V-2DDT : accessed 31 July 2026), entry for Birte Christensd and Christen Nielsen, 18 Apr 1819.

localities.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Tyrsted Parish, Vejle, Denmark (c. 1780–1820)

## Jurisdiction History
Tyrsted (Danish: Tyrsted Sogn) is a Lutheran parish in east Jutland. Its jurisdictional history across the target period:
- **Until 1793**: Under Stjernholm amt (county). Parish register era-volume: 1684–1796.
- **1793–1970**: Under Hatting herred (district), Vejle amt. New parish register series begins 1793.
- **1970–2006**: Reorganized as Tyrsted, Horsens, Vejle.

For the nine known children (b. 1791–1801) and the putative 1805 daughter, records fall across both the Stjernholm-era and Vejle-era volumes.

## Parish Registers (Kirkebøger) — Primary Source

FamilySearch has digitized four Tyrsted volumes covering 1684–1829:

| Image Group | Coverage | Images | Indexed | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 007226375_001_M9DY-VF3 | 1684–1796 | 212 | **0%** | Browse-only |
| 007226375_002_M9DY-VFQ | **1793–1823** | 131 | **43%** | Partial index + browse |
| 007226375_003_M9DY-VF7 | 1814–1829 | 75 | 91% | Indexed |
| 007226375_004_M9DY-VFW | 1814–1829 | 37 | 35% | Partial index |

The **1793–1823 volume** (007226375_002) is the primary target for the 1805 baptism question. It is 43% indexed in **Denmark, Baptisms, 1618-1923** (FamilySearch collection 1778463), which holds **2,633 Tyrsted records**. The wiki article 'Vejle County Denmark Baptisms Coverage Table' confirms this count. The unindexed ~57% must be browsed image by image.

For births 1791–1793, the Stjernholm-era volume (007226375_001, 0% indexed) must be browsed directly via FamilySearch or Arkivalieronline (arkivalieronline.rigsarkivet.dk — free access to Danish church books).

**Also available:** Denmark, Church Records, 1484-1941 (collection 2078555, index + images) — broad collection covering baptisms, marriages, and burials.

## Census Records
- **1787 census** (FamilySearch collection 2790466, indexed): Will show Chresten Nielsen's household before the children's births.
- **1801 census** (NOT on FamilySearch — use Ancestry collection 61726 or Danish State Archives sa.dk): Shows household composition between the known children and the putative 1805 birth. Also available via Danish Demographic Database (ddd.dda.dk).
- **1834, 1840+ censuses** (FamilySearch, indexed): Too late for the primary question but may help confirm later family composition.

## Burial Records
- **Denmark, Burials, 1640-1917** (FamilySearch collection 1520593, indexed): Search for a Birte Nielsdatter who died in infancy or childhood in Tyrsted, which would explain absence from later records.

## Marriage Records
- **Denmark, Marriages, 1635-1916** (FamilySearch collection 1520592, indexed): Not primary for this question but useful for confirming Chresten and Birte Kirstine's marriage and for any daughter Birte who later married.

## Military Records
- **Military Conscription Rolls, 1789-1793** (FamilySearch collection 2243379, indexed): May help locate/confirm Chresten Nielsen's identity and residence. Also: Lægdsruller 1743-1862 (FamilySearch catalog 448204, images).

## Probate / Estate Records
- **Denmark, Probate Indexes, 1674-1851** (FamilySearch collection 2026233, indexed): Estate record for Chresten Nielsen or Birte Kirstine could enumerate heirs/children.
- **Arkivalieronline**: broader access to Danish probate and estate records.

## Key Online Repositories
- **FamilySearch.org**: Primary — indexed collections + image volumes
- **Arkivalieronline** (arkivalieronline.rigsarkivet.dk): Free Danish State Archives portal — images of church books, probate, census
- **Dansk Demografisk Database** (ddd.dda.dk): Links census and other records
- **Link-lives.dk**: Links individuals across 1787–1901 census records
- **Ancestry.com** ($): 1801 census, church records 1812–1924, marriages
- **DIS-Arkivalielister** (arkivalielister.dis-danmark.dk): Military levying rolls index

## Language and Handwriting
Records are in Danish (and occasionally Latin in the 18th century). Handwriting is old Danish Kurrent script. FamilySearch provides a Denmark Handwriting guide. Daughters of Chresten Nielsen would be recorded as **Nielsdatter**, not Nielsen — essential for record searches.

## Research Strategy for q_001
1. **Search indexed baptisms first**: 'Denmark, Baptisms, 1618-1923' (collection 1778463), filtered to Tyrsted, Vejle, c. 1804–1807, father = Chresten Nielsen. Also try 'Denmark, Church Records, 1484-1941' (2078555).
2. **Browse the unindexed portion** of imageGroup 007226375_002_M9DY-VFQ (1793–1823) via FamilySearch or Arkivalieronline if the indexed search returns no 1805 Birte.
3. **Browse the 1791–1793 births** in imageGroup 007226375_001_M9DY-VF3 to verify the nine known children as a foundation.
4. **Check 1801 census** (Ancestry/sa.dk) for household composition — presence/absence of a Birte in 1801 informs whether a c. 1805 birth is plausible.
5. **Search burial records** for a Birte Nielsdatter in Tyrsted, c. 1805–1825, to explain absence from later records if the baptism is found but the daughter doesn't appear in 1834+ censuses.
